IF A SKILL APPLIES TO YOUR TASK, YOU DO NOT HAVE A CHOICE. YOU MUST USE IT.

## The Rule

**Invoke relevant or requested skills BEFORE any response or action** — including clarifying questions, exploring the codebase, or checking files. If it turns out wrong for the situation, you don't have to use it.

**Before entering plan mode:** if you haven't already brainstormed, invoke the brainstorming skill first.

Then announce "Using [skill] to [purpose]" and follow the skill exactly. If it has a checklist, create a todo per item.

## Skill Priority

When multiple skills apply, process skills come first — they set the approach, then implementation skills (frontend-design, etc.) carry it out. Brainstorming and systematic-debugging are Superpowers' most common process skills, but the rule holds for any of them.

- "Let's build X" → superpowers:brainstorming first, then implementation skills.
- "Fix this bug" → superpowers:systematic-debugging first, then domain skills.

## Red Flags

These thoughts mean STOP—you're rationalizing:

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is just a simple question" | Questions are tasks. Check for skills. |
| "I need more context first" | Skill check comes BEFORE clarifying questions. |
| "Let me explore the codebase first" | Skills tell you HOW to explore. Check first. |
| "I can check git/files quickly" | Files lack conversation context. Check for skills. |
| "Let me gather information first" | Skills tell you HOW to gather information. |
| "This doesn't need a formal skill" | If a skill exists, use it. |
| "I remember this skill" | Skills evolve. Read current version. |
| "This doesn't count as a task" | Action = task. Check for skills. |
| "The skill is overkill" | Simple things become complex. Use it. |
| "I'll just do this one thing first" | Check BEFORE doing anything. |
| "This feels productive" | Undisciplined action wastes time. Skills prevent this. |
| "I know what that means" | Knowing the concept ≠ using the skill. Invoke it. |

## Platform Adaptation

If your harness appears here, read its reference file for special instructions:

- Codex: `references/codex-tools.md`
- Pi: `references/pi-tools.md`
- Antigravity: `references/antigravity-tools.md`

## User Instructions

User instructions (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, etc, direct requests) take precedence over skills, which in turn override default behavior. Only skip skill workflows or instructions when your human partner has explicitly told you to.
</EXTREMELY_IMPORTANT>"

The original narrow bands (work `[3,4.5]`, evening 100 `[3.5,5]`) baked one assumed dress code in for everyone, so a smart-casual wardrobe could not produce a 101 Work or Evening outfit **at all** — the screen just said "Add a few more pieces" with 8 items in the closet. 102 103 The resolution order is now: **occasion band → narrowed by the profile's dress codes → overridden by Refine.** 104 105 - Bands widened (`lib/generator/rules.ts`); every band includes 3 (smart casual). 106 - `personalBand()` intersects with `profiles.formality_min/max` — the answer onboarding **already 107 collected** and the generator had never selected. Fixed: shoes get a wider formality floor (1.0 vs 0.5 — a clean sneaker is 114 valid smart-casual work wear); outerwear is no longer *required* below 15° (that gave anyone without a 115 coat nothing all winter). Empty results now name the blocking slot via `missingCategory()`. 116 117 **⚠️ The same pattern remains in `seasons`** — it's still a hard filter. Either soften the seasons filter the way 120 outerwear was softened, or treat it as a tagging problem. Not yet decided. 121 122 ### Deliberate divergence from the design handoff: the occasion row 123 124 `generator-mockup-v2.html:96` specifies a scrolling chip row with a right-edge gradient fade 125 (`-webkit-mask-image`) and the Refine pill inside the row. The 34% figure is desktop-only 137 and misled the first review; see memory `mobile-first-evaluate-at-phone-width`. 138 139 **Changed:** `OccasionRow` is now a non-scrolling `flex-1` row of four chips (13px labels), and Refine 140 moved to the header beside "Today's Looks" as `RefineButton`. Refine is a *modifier* on the chosen 141 occasion, not a fifth peer of it, so the header is also the more honest hierarchy. Coords are now rounded to 2dp (~1.1km) at the fetch boundary and 168 before persisting — also less precise personal data stored. 169 - **A chosen city was clobbered** by the silent refresh on every load (race + the stored `location_source` 170 never being read back). Fixed in `ca3c1bd`; see decision L8 in the spec. 171 4. **Re-onboard to re-test** — local DB was reset this session, so all local data (user + items) is wiped. Sign 172 in (email magic-link via Mailpit `http://127.0.0.1:54324`) → quiz → capture a few items → `/generate`. 173 Note: an oxford at formality 4 won't fit "Everyday" [1.5,3]; tag it 3 for a valid Everyday combo. 174 5. **Roadmap (Plans 07–13):** outfit detail · Style DNA · OOTD calendar/diary · saved outfits · profile hub · 175 wear stats · share cards. This **wiped local data**. (Alternative non-destructive fix: refresh collation on the 187 volume; the user chose the reset.) 188 - **`42501` permission denied on every write** after the reset: the newer Supabase DB image no longer 189 auto-grants table DML to `authenticated`, and our migrations never granted it explicitly (they relied on the 190 old default privileges). **Fixed** by migration `20260721090000_authenticated_grants.sql` (grants 191 SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on all public tables to `authenticated` + default privileges for future tables). 192 RLS still restricts rows. **This must be committed.** 193 194 ## How to resume (services) 195 196 ```bash 197 set -a; source .env.local; set +a && supabase start # env needed for Google OAuth config.toml env() 198 npm run dev # :3000 199 ``` 200 Supabase is currently **running** (fresh DB, migrations applied incl. the grants fix). Mailpit `:54324`, 201 Studio `:54323`. If `supabase start` ever fails on the collation error again, see the gotcha above. 202 203 --- 204 205 ## Key decisions + preferences established (also in memory) 206 207 - **No AI attribution anywhere** — commits, PR bodies, any shared artifact. Overrides the harness default. 208 (memory `no-ai-attribution`) 209 - **Prefer the future-proof option at architecture forks**, not the minimal diff. (memory 210 `prefer-future-proof-architecture`) — e.g. the `useCapture` engine extraction; the layout-template system. 211 - **Meta/authorship docs stay OUT of git** (`CLAUDE.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `PRODUCT.md`, `docs/`, `.impeccable/`, 212 `fitcheck-complete-spec.md` all gitignored). **Functional AI product code STAYS** (`lib/ai`, `@anthropic-ai/sdk`, 213 `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`). History was NOT rewritten to purge CLAUDE.md. 214 - **Split builds into small per-feature TDD plans** (memory `prefer-multiple-scoped-plans`). 215 - Stack: Next 16 (proxy not middleware) · React 19 · Tailwind v4 (Midnight Atelier tokens wired) · `motion` · 216 Supabase (RLS) · Haiku 4.5 via `output_config.format` + `forStructuredOutput` (strip validation keywords) · 217 Open-Meteo (no key) · Zod 4. 218 219 ## Pointers 220 - Generator plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-18-stylist-generator.md` 221 - Design spec: `design_handoff_stylist_generator/README.md` + `generator-mockup-v2.html` 222 - Product/roadmap: `fitcheck-complete-spec.md` · `docs/prototype-review.md` 223 - Design system: `DESIGN.md` / `PRODUCT.md` (local-only) 224

Base directory for this skill: /Users/1curafu/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.1.1/skills/writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write comprehensive implementation plans assuming the engineer has zero context for our codebase and questionable taste. Document everything they need to know: which files to touch for each task, code, testing, docs they might need to check, how to test it. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

Assume they are a skilled developer, but know almost nothing about our toolset or problem domain. Assume they don't know good test design very well.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Bite-Sized Task Granularity

**Each step is one action (2-5 minutes):**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Write minimal implementation**

```python
def function(input):
    return expected
```

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## No Placeholders

Every step must contain the actual content an engineer needs. These are **plan failures** — never write them:
- "TBD", "TODO", "implement later", "fill in details"
- "Add appropriate error handling" / "add validation" / "handle edge cases"
- "Write tests for the above" (without actual test code)
- "Similar to Task N" (repeat the code — the engineer may be reading tasks out of order)
- Steps that describe what to do without showing how (code blocks required for code steps)
- References to types, functions, or methods not defined in any task

## Remember
- Exact file paths always
- Complete code in every step — if a step changes code, show the code
- Exact commands with expected output
- DRY, YAGNI, TDD, frequent commits

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Placeholder scan:** Search your plan for red flags — any of the patterns from the "No Placeholders" section above. Fix them.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving the plan, offer execution choice:

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Two execution options:**

**1. Subagent-Driven (recommended)** - I dispatch a fresh subagent per task, review between tasks, fast iteration

**2. Inline Execution** - Execute tasks in this session using executing-plans, batch execution with checkpoints

**Which approach?"**

**If Subagent-Driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development
- Fresh subagent per task + two-stage review

**If Inline Execution chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans
- Batch execution with checkpoints for review

Plan written: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-24-seasons-soft-preference.md`

**The shape of the fix** — season stops being able to veto anything, in three moves:

1. **`lib/generator/season.ts`** (new) — `inSeason` / `seasonFit` / `currentSeason` in one place, case-insensitive (production stores `"Winter"`, your fixtures use `"winter"` — that mismatch is one bad refactor away from being a live bug).
2. **`candidates.ts`** — delete the filter line, and sort each category **in-season-first** before the triple loop. That second half matters: `buildCandidates` caps at 200 combos *before* scoring, so without the sort a big off-season closet could push the good combos past the cap and quietly undo the preference. Bonus — `outer[0]` and `accessories[0]` now grab the seasonally right piece.
3. **`score.ts`** — a `SEASON_WEIGHT = 0.2` term, built exactly like `LEAN_WEIGHT`: zero weight when no season is passed, so existing scores stay byte-identical.

**Two things I want to flag rather than bury:**

- Removing the filter removes an *incidental* protection — a wool sweater tagged `{Autumn,Winter}` can now surface in July if the closet is thin. That's consistent with `personalBand`'s existing "better a slightly-off outfit than none", and ranking buries it whenever anything better exists. The proper fix is a heat-based material exclusion in `weatherRules` (measured, not calendar-derived) — I scoped it as an explicit follow-up, not part of this change.
- `currentSeason` **has** to move out of `app/generate/actions.ts` — it's a `"use server"` module, so it can only export async functions, which is why that helper was never testable.

The plan also notes honestly that the December case is proven by unit tests, not the live run — the server reads the real clock and I didn't add a date override for it.

Two ways to run it:

1. **Subagent-driven** (recommended) — fresh subagent per task, I review between each.
2. **Inline** — I execute here with checkpoints.

content.text:
Mostly yes — but you've made me look at one thing in it I'd now change.

**Where I'm confident:** removing the veto is right. A signal derived from the calendar month should not be able to zero a required slot when we already measure the actual weather. And soft-preference is the pattern this codebase has converged on twice already (outerwear, colour lean), both times after the same failure — a hard filter producing a silent dead end. A third instance of the same lesson should get the same treatment.

**The alternative worth naming:** per-slot fallback — keep the filter, but if a required category comes up empty, drop the season constraint *for that category only*. It's about five lines and gives you *strict* seasonality whenever the closet can afford it. I still prefer scoring, because the fallback is binary: one winter top and ten summer tops means all three of the day's looks share that one top. Scoring gives you variety with a seasonal bias. But it's a genuine trade, not an obvious win.

**Where my plan is actually weak** — and this is the part I'd fix: it *removes* a protection and defers the replacement. Today, the season filter is the only thing keeping a wool sweater out of a 30°C July outfit. After this change, only a 0.2 scoring weight discourages it, and I parked the real fix ("heat-based material exclusion in `weatherRules`") as a follow-up. Follow-ups don't always happen. `weatherRules` is currently asymmetric anyway — it handles cold (`tempC < 15` → layer) and rain (excludes suede) but has nothing for heat:

```ts
return {
  needsOuterwear: w.tempC < 15,
  excludeMaterials: w.rain ? ["suede", "canvas"] : [],
};
```

Adding heat exclusions there is a handful of lines, uses the temperature we already fetch, and means the PR replaces a coarse protection with a measured one instead of just deleting it. That's a better-shaped change than two PRs where the second is optional.

The other open number is `SEASON_WEIGHT = 0.2`. It only reorders when combos score within 0.2 of each other, so in a rich closet a slightly-more-harmonious linen shirt can still beat a wool one in January. I picked it to sit under the existing `LEAN_WEIGHT = 0.3`; it's a guess that wants checking against a real closet.

## The protection this replaces (state this in the PR body)

Deleting the hard filter also deletes an incidental protection: the season tag was the only thing keeping a wool sweater out of a 30°C July outfit. So this plan does not merely delete it — **Task 4 replaces it with the measured equivalent**: `weatherRules` gains heat-based material exclusions, driven by the temperature we already fetch. +### Task 4: The measured replacement — heat exclusions + material relief

+This is the task that keeps the change honest: it replaces the thermal protection Task 3 removed with one driven by the actual temperature, and makes that safe by guaranteeing no weather exclusion can empty a required slot.
**Files:**
+- Modify: `lib/generator/rules.ts` (`weatherRules`, at the end of the file)
+- Modify: `lib/generator/candidates.ts` (`isEligible`, `eligibility`, `buildCandidates`)
+- Test: `lib/generator/__tests__/rules.test.ts` (append), `lib/generator/__tests__/candidates.test.ts` (append)

+- Produces: `weatherRules(w)` return type is unchanged (`{ needsOuterwear: boolean; excludeMaterials: string[] }`). New internal export in candidates: `eligibleByCategory(items: CandidateItem[], a: CandidateArgs): Record<string, CandidateItem[]>`. `eligibility` and `missingCategory` keep their existing signatures.
+**Two decisions baked in here:**
+- **Threshold `tempC > 25`.** Strictly above 25 so the existing `summer` fixture (`tempC: 24`) keeps its current meaning — 24°C is pleasant, 26°C is properly hot.

+- **Substring matching.** Today `excludeMaterials.includes(i.material.toLowerCase())` is an exact match, so a rain day already fails to exclude `"suede leather"`, and `"merino wool"` would slip past a heat rule. Matching by substring makes both rules actually bite.
+- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing weather-rule test**
+Append to `lib/generator/__tests__/rules.test.ts`:
+test("real heat excludes warm materials — the measured version of the old season filter", () => {
+  const hot = weatherRules({ tempC: 30, rain: false }).excludeMaterials;
+  expect(hot).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["wool", "fleece", "cashmere"]));
+test("a pleasant day excludes nothing — the threshold is properly hot, not merely warm", () => {
+  expect(weatherRules({ tempC: 24, rain: false }).excludeMaterials).toEqual([]);
+  expect(weatherRules({ tempC: 25, rain: false }).excludeMaterials).toEqual([]);
+test("a hot rainy day excludes both sets", () => {
+  const both = weatherRules({ tempC: 30, rain: true }).excludeMaterials;
+  expect(both).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["suede", "canvas", "wool"]));
+test("cold days are unaffected by the heat rule", () => {
+  expect(weatherRules({ tempC: 5, rain: false }).excludeMaterials).toEqual([]);
+  expect(weatherRules({ tempC: 5, rain: false }).needsOuterwear).toBe(true);
+- [ ] **Step 2: Run it to verify it fails**

+- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the heat rule**
+Replace `weatherRules` at the end of `lib/generator/rules.ts`:
+ * Materials that make a properly hot day unpleasant. This is the MEASURED
+ * replacement for the season tag's incidental thermal protection: season used to
+ * be a hard filter, so a wool sweater tagged {Autumn,Winter} could never reach a
+ * July outfit. Season is now a preference (see ./season.ts), so the guard moved
+ * here — to the temperature we already fetch, which is a real reading of the day
+ * rather than a label derived from the calendar month.
+const HOT_MATERIALS = ["wool", "cashmere", "fleece", "shearling", "tweed", "corduroy", "down"];
+/** Strictly above 25: 24° is pleasant, 26° is hot. */
+const HOT_C = 25;
+export function weatherRules(w: Weather) {
+  return {
+    needsOuterwear: w.tempC < 15,
+    excludeMaterials: [
+      ...(w.rain ? ["suede", "canvas"] : []),
+      ...(w.tempC > HOT_C ? HOT_MATERIALS : []),

+// pre-existing dead end: a closet whose only shoes were suede returned zero
+// outfits in the rain, with the empty screen blaming "Shoes".

+  { id: "b1", category: "Bottoms", colors: ["navy"], formality: 3, seasons: ["Spring"], material: "cotton" },
+  { id: "s1", category: "Shoes", colors: ["tan"], formality: 3, seasons: ["Spring"], material: "suede" },

+function materialExcluded(material: string | null, excludeMaterials: string[]): boolean {

+  // "suede leather" are real values that an exact match silently let through.

+  // required slot, so one narrowly-tagged category zeroed the whole result.

Folded in as **Task 4** — the plan is now 6 tasks. What changed:

**`weatherRules` gains heat**, replacing rather than deleting the protection:
```ts
excludeMaterials: [
  ...(w.rain ? ["suede", "canvas"] : []),
  ...(w.tempC > 25 ? HOT_MATERIALS : []),   // wool, cashmere, fleece, shearling, tweed, corduroy, down
]
```
Threshold is strictly above 25 so your existing `summer` fixture (`tempC: 24`) keeps its current meaning.

**Material matching moves from equality to substring.** This turned up while writing it: today's check is `excludeMaterials.includes(i.material.toLowerCase())` — an exact match. The tagger writes free text, so `"merino wool"` and `"suede leather"` already slip through the *rain* rule. Exact matching would have made the heat rule mostly decorative.

**The part I didn't expect to find:** adding a heat list would have multiplied a dead end that's already in there. `excludeMaterials` is a hard filter on every slot, so a closet whose only shoes are suede **already** returns zero outfits in the rain and blames "Shoes" — the same bug class we're fixing, just triggered by weather instead of season. So Task 4 applies one rule to both: *a weather exclusion may narrow a required slot but never empty it* — if it would, that slot is refilled without the exclusion. Formality gaps are untouched, since those are real wardrobe gaps worth reporting.

That required a small consolidation: `eligibility`, `missingCategory` and `buildCandidates` now all read from one `eligibleByCategory`, so they can't disagree about what the closet can do. Previously nothing structurally prevented `missingCategory` saying "Shoes" while `buildCandidates` happily produced combos.

Same two options:

1. **Subagent-driven** (recommended) — fresh subagent per task, I review between each.
2. **Inline** — I execute here with checkpoints.

=== docs/plans === 00-overview.md 01-setup.md 02-auth.md 03-design-system.md 04-upload-pipeline.md 05-closet.md 06-generator.md === BUGS.md === # Bug Report — Code Review 2026-07-04 > Scope: everything on `feat/auth-onboarding` vs `main` + uncommitted work (plans 02–05). > 16 findings, ranked most-severe first. All verified against the code; the structured-outputs > claim also verified against the Anthropic API docs (claude-api skill). > > **Headline:** the capture→tagging pipeline (plan 04) is broken by bugs #1–#3 stacked on top of > each other — adding `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` alone will NOT make capture work. Fix #1–#4 first, > then e2e-test capture. --- ## 🔴 Critical — capture pipeline blockers ### 1. Tagging schema is rejected by the Anthropic API (every call 400s) **Where:** `lib/ai/tagging-schema.ts:17` + `lib/ai/tag-item.ts:21` **Bug:** `taggingJsonSchema = z.toJSONSchema(TagSchema)` is passed raw into `output_config.format`. The raw output contains JSON Schema constraints that Anthropic structured outputs **does not support** and rejects with `400 invalid_request_error`: - `minLength: 1` (subcategory, material) - `minItems: 1` / `maxItems: 3` (colors, seasons) - `minimum: 1` / `maximum: 5` (formality) Only the SDK helpers strip these client-side; this code uses neither. Result: once the API key is set, **every capture fails at the tagging step, always.** **Fix:** use the SDK's Zod helper — it strips unsupported constraints before sending and validates the response against the Zod schema (also replaces the hand-rolled `parseTagText` in `lib/ai/parse-tags.ts`): ```ts import { zodOutputFormat } from "@anthropic-ai/sdk/helpers/zod"; const res = await client.messages.parse({ model: "claude-haiku-4-5", max_tokens: 512, output_config: { format: zodOutputFormat(TagSchema) }, messages: [ /* unchanged */ ], }); const tags = res.parsed_output; // already validated Tags | null — guard for null ``` --- ### 2. Server Action payload exceeds Next's 1 MB body limit for typical photos **Where:** `components/capture/capture-flow.tsx:45` (+ `next.config.ts` sets no override) **Bug:** `uploadAndTag` sends **two base64 images** in one Server Action body. The compressed original is up to 0.5 MB (≈0.67 MB as base64); the @imgly cutout is a 1280px PNG **with alpha and no size cap** — routinely 0.5–3 MB (+33 % base64). Combined payload exceeds the default `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` of 1 MB → `"Body exceeded 1 MB limit"` → "Capture failed" for most real photos. **Fix (quick):** raise the limit in `next.config.ts`: ```ts const nextConfig: NextConfig = { experimental: { serverActions: { bodySizeLimit: "8mb" } }, }; ``` **Fix (better, do eventually):** upload both blobs **client-side** directly to Supabase Storage (`supabase.storage.from("wardrobe").upload(...)` with the browser client — the storage RLS policy already scopes writes to `auth.uid()`), then pass only the two paths to the action. Kills the base64 inflation, the body limit, and bug #4's server-side blind spot in one move. --- ### 3. Module-scope `new Anthropic()` crashes the whole upload module without an API key **Where:** `lib/ai/tag-item.ts:7` **Bug:** `const client = new Anthropic()` runs at module init. With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` blank (its current state in `.env.local`), importing `app/closet/upload/actions.ts` throws `Could not resolve apiKey` — so **both** actions 500, including `confirmItem`, which needs no AI at all. Even saving an already-tagged draft is impossible. **Fix:** construct lazily inside `tagItem`: ```ts let client: Anthropic | null = null; export async function tagItem(...) { client ??= new Anthropic(); // fails only here, only when tagging ... } ``` --- ### 4. Storage upload errors are silently swallowed → items with permanently missing images **Where:** `app/closet/upload/actions.ts:27-32` **Bug:** `supabase.storage.upload()` **returns** `{ error }` — it does not throw. Both calls discard the result. If either upload fails (RLS rejection, missing bucket, transient network/5xx), the action still tags and returns paths; the user confirms; `confirmItem` inserts an items row pointing at objects that don't exist. The photo is lost forever — the closet renders a blank card with no recovery except delete + re-capture. **Fix:** ```ts const { error: origErr } = await supabase.storage .from("wardrobe").upload(`${base}/original.jpg`, orig, { contentType: "image/jpeg" }); if (origErr) throw new Error(`Upload failed: ${origErr.message}`); const { error: cutErr } = await supabase.storage .from("wardrobe").upload(`${base}/cutout.png`, cut, { contentType: "image/png" }); if (cutErr) throw new Error(`Upload failed: ${cutErr.message}`); ``` --- ## 🟠 High — broken user-facing flows ### 5. Two of four bottom-nav tabs 404 **Where:** `components/shell/mobile-nav.tsx:12-13` **Bug:** nav links to `/generate` (Stylist) and `/calendar` (Diary), but neither route exists (`app/` only has `auth`, `closet`, `onboarding`, `profile`). Tapping either lands on Next's 404 page, which has no MobileNav — only browser-back recovers. **Fix (until plans 06/09 land):** add stub routes with a "coming soon" screen inside the mobile shell (mirroring the old closet stub), **or** render those tabs disabled/ghosted. Delete the stubs when plan 06 (generator) and plan 09 (calendar) are built. ### 6. Auth failure is silently invisible **Where:** `app/auth/callback/route.ts:24` + `app/page.tsx` **Bug:** on `exchangeCodeForSession` failure the callback redirects to `/?error=auth`, but `app/page.tsx` never reads `searchParams` — the user lands on the welcome screen with zero feedback. Classic trigger: opening the magic link in a different browser than the one that requested it (PKCE verifier cookie missing) or an expired link. Retrying loops silently. **Fix:** read the param in the Welcome page and render a notice: ```tsx export default async function Welcome({ searchParams, }: { searchParams: Promise<{ error?: string }> }) { const { error } = await searchParams; ... {error === "auth" && (

Sign-in link expired or was opened in a different browser. Please request a new one.

)} } ``` --- ## 🟡 Medium — data integrity & conventions ### 7. Item detail Save fabricates data on cleared fields **Where:** `components/closet/item-detail.tsx:61-63` **Bug:** empty material is silently written as `"Unknown"`; empty seasons becomes `["Spring"]` — so a user who deselects all seasons gets an item the generator will exclude 9 months a year, with no feedback. The capture confirm screen handles the same case differently (blocks deselecting the last season) — two screens disagree on one operation. **Fix:** reuse the capture flow's guard — in `toggleSeason`, refuse to remove the last selected season; require non-empty material before enabling Save (or keep the previous value instead of substituting "Unknown"). ### 8. `original.jpg` stores non-JPEG bytes with a JPEG content type **Where:** `app/closet/upload/actions.ts:27` + `lib/images/options.ts` **Bug:** `browser-image-compression` preserves the input MIME type (no `fileType` set), so a PNG/WebP library photo is uploaded as PNG/WebP bytes under `original.jpg` with `contentType: "image/jpeg"`. Permanent mislabel (originals are captured once); bites any consumer that trusts the declared type (Phase-2 share cards, exports, re-tagging). **Fix:** force JPEG in `lib/images/options.ts`: ```ts export function compressionOptions() { return { maxSizeMB: 0.5, maxWidthOrHeight: 1280, useWebWorker: true, fileType: "image/jpeg" }; } ``` ### 9. CLAUDE.md violation: colors / pattern / subcategory are not user-editable **Where:** `app/closet/[itemId]/actions.ts:9` (UpdateSchema) + both edit screens **Bug:** CLAUDE.md mandates *"Tags are always user-editable — treat AI tags as a draft."* When Haiku mis-tags colors or pattern (the ~10 % case the confirm screen exists for), the user cannot fix them anywhere — and wrong colors will directly poison the plan-06 color- harmony scoring. **Fix:** add `colors`, `pattern`, `subcategory` to `UpdateSchema` and expose editors — colors as chip multi-select (curated palette), pattern as the 5-value chip row — on both the capture confirm screen and item detail. ### 10. CLAUDE.md violation: no RLS tenant tests **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20260615114702_items.sql:23` **Bug:** CLAUDE.md conventions: *"RLS: every table … Add tenant tests."* The items table + wardrobe storage policies shipped with a full Vitest harness in the same diff but zero tests asserting user A cannot read user B's items/objects. A future policy edit that opens cross-tenant reads ships silently. **Fix:** add an integration test against local Supabase: create two users, insert an item as A, assert B's client gets zero rows from `items` and a 403/empty from signing A's storage path. (Plan 00's testing approach already calls for exactly this.) ### 11. Apple OAuth `env()` references may break `supabase start` (plausible, env-dependent) **Where:** `supabase/config.toml:276-278` **Bug:** the **disabled** Apple block uses `env(SUPABASE_AUTH_EXTERNAL_APPLE_CLIENT_ID)` / `env(...APPLE_SECRET)`. Some Supabase CLI versions error on unset env() references at config parse even when `enabled = false`. A contributor sourcing only the documented Google vars may fail `supabase start`. **Fix:** while disabled, use literal empty strings (`client_id = ""`, `secret = ""`) and restore the `env()` form when Apple ships — or add both vars (blank) to `.env.local` + LOCAL_DEV.md. Verify with a clean-env `supabase start` first; skip if your CLI version tolerates it. --- ## 🟢 Lower priority — hygiene, efficiency, dead code ### 12. Orphaned storage objects on abandoned captures **Where:** `app/closet/upload/actions.ts:22` Images are uploaded **before** confirm with no cleanup path. Every abandoned capture or tagging failure leaks two objects, forever — unbounded storage growth and invisible data for the GDPR deletion pipeline. **Fix:** upload at confirm time (natural if you take bug #2's "better" fix), or write drafts under a `drafts/` prefix that a scheduled cleanup expires. ### 13. Serial awaits on the magic-moment path **Where:** `app/closet/upload/actions.ts:27-34` The two uploads and the tagging call are mutually independent (`tagItem` uses `cutoutB64` from memory) but run sequentially — several avoidable seconds on the spinner. **Fix:** `await Promise.all([uploadOriginal, uploadCutout, tagItem(...)])` (checking each result per bug #4). Same pattern in `app/closet/[itemId]/page.tsx:28` — the brands query can run in `Promise.all` with the item fetch. ### 14. Domain vocabulary triplicated **Where:** `components/capture/capture-flow.tsx:11-17`, `components/closet/item-detail.tsx:10-16`, `components/closet/closet-grid.tsx:8` `CATEGORIES` / `SEASONS` / `FORMALITY_LABEL` / 14-entry `MATERIALS` are copy-pasted across three files and will drift. **Fix:** derive categories/seasons from `TagSchema` enums (`TagSchema.shape.category.options`) in one shared module, e.g. `lib/closet/vocab.ts`. ### 15. Dead filter logic **Where:** `lib/closet/filter.ts:13` `filterItems` re-checks `archived` client-side though every caller already queries `.eq("archived", false)`, and the `color` filter param has no consumer. **Fix:** reduce it to the category match it actually performs (and its tests along with it). ### 16. Unused motion variants lock in a dead dependency **Where:** `lib/motion.ts:4` `fcRise` / `fcFade` / `fcPop` have zero runtime consumers — only the test imports them, so the suite green-lights an export surface that can silently rot. **Fix:** wire the variants into the shipped screens (capture confirm, closet grid entrances — plan 03 intended this) or drop the module + test until a consumer lands. --- ## Suggested fix order 1. **#1 + #3** (`tag-item.ts` / `tagging-schema.ts`) — one edit session, makes tagging callable 2. **#4** (upload error checks) — 5 lines 3. **#2** (body size limit — quick fix now, client-side upload later) 4. → **e2e-test capture with the API key** (the original next step in STATE.md) 5. **#5, #6, #7** — user-facing polish, each small 6. **#9, #10** — CLAUDE.md compliance (colors editable, tenant tests) 7. **#8, #11–#16** — opportunistic, or fold into plan-06 prep *Not bugs, but open scope from STATE.md: onboarding 5-item capture (plan 04 task 9) not built; `/onboarding` doesn't redirect already-onboarded users away; plan 06 (generator) not started.*

Item detail Save fabricates data on cleared fields **Where:** `components/closet/item-detail.tsx:61-63` **Bug:** empty material is silently written as `"Unknown"`; empty seasons becomes `["Spring"]` — so a user who deselects all seasons gets an item the generator will exclude 9 months a year, with no feedback. The capture confirm screen handles the same case differently (blocks deselecting the last season) — two screens disagree on one operation. **Fix:** reuse the capture flow's guard — in `toggleSeason`, refuse to remove the last selected season; require non-empty material before enabling Save (or keep the previous value instead of substituting "Unknown"). ### 8. `original.jpg` stores non-JPEG bytes with a JPEG content type **Where:** `app/closet/upload/actions.ts:27` + `lib/images/options.ts` **Bug:** `browser-image-compression` preserves the input MIME type (no `fileType` set), so a PNG/WebP library photo is uploaded as PNG/WebP bytes under `original.jpg` with `contentType: "image/jpeg"`. Permanent mislabel (originals are captured once); bites any consumer that trusts the declared type (Phase-2 share cards, exports, re-tagging). **Fix:** force JPEG in `lib/images/options.ts`: ```ts export function compressionOptions() { return { maxSizeMB: 0.5, maxWidthOrHeight: 1280, useWebWorker: true, fileType: "image/jpeg" }; } ``` ### 9. CLAUDE.md violation: colors / pattern / subcategory are not user-editable **Where:** `app/closet/[itemId]/actions.ts:9` (UpdateSchema) + both edit screens **Bug:** CLAUDE.md mandates *"Tags are always user-editable — treat AI tags as a draft."* When Haiku mis-tags colors or pattern (the ~10 % case the confirm screen exists for), the user cannot fix them anywhere — and wrong colors will directly poison the plan-06 color- harmony scoring. **Fix:** add `colors`, `pattern`, `subcategory` to `UpdateSchema` and expose editors — colors as chip multi-select (curated palette), pattern as the 5-value chip row — on both the capture confirm screen and item detail. ### 10. CLAUDE.md violation: no RLS tenant tests **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20260615114702_items.sql:23` **Bug:** CLAUDE.md conventions: *"RLS: every table … Add tenant tests."* The items table + wardrobe storage policies shipped with a full Vitest harness in the same diff but zero tests asserting user A cannot read user B's items/objects. A future policy edit that opens cross-tenant reads ships silently. **Fix:** add an integration test against local Supabase: create two users, insert an item as A, assert B's client gets zero rows from `items` and a 403/empty from signing A's storage path. (Plan 00's testing approach already calls for exactly this.) ### 11. Apple OAuth `env()` references may break `supabase start` (plausible, env-dependent) **Where:** `supabase/config.toml:276-278` **Bug:** the **disabled** Apple block uses `env(SUPABASE_AUTH_EXTERNAL_APPLE_CLIENT_ID)` / `env(...APPLE_SECRET)`. Some Supabase CLI versions error on unset env() references at config parse even when `enabled = false`. A contributor sourcing only the documented Google vars may fail `supabase start`. **Fix:** while disabled, use literal empty strings (`client_id = ""`, `secret = ""`) and restore the `env()` form when Apple ships — or add both vars (blank) to `.env.local` + LOCAL_DEV.md. Verify with a clean-env `supabase start` first; skip if your CLI version tolerates it. --- ## 🟢 Lower priority — hygiene, efficiency, dead code ### 12. Orphaned storage objects on abandoned captures **Where:** `app/closet/upload/actions.ts:22` Images are uploaded **before** confirm with no cleanup path. Every abandoned capture or tagging failure leaks two objects, forever — unbounded storage growth and invisible data for the GDPR deletion pipeline. **Fix:** upload at confirm time (natural if you take bug #2's "better" fix), or write drafts under a `drafts/` prefix that a scheduled cleanup expires. ### 13. Serial awaits on the magic-moment path **Where:** `app/closet/upload/actions.ts:27-34` The two uploads and the tagging call are mutually independent (`tagItem` uses `cutoutB64` from memory) but run sequentially — several avoidable seconds on the spinner. **Fix:** `await Promise.all([uploadOriginal, uploadCutout, tagItem(...)])` (checking each result per bug #4). Same pattern in `app/closet/[itemId]/page.tsx:28` — the brands query can run in `Promise.all` with the item fetch. ### 14. Domain vocabulary triplicated **Where:** `components/capture/capture-flow.tsx:11-17`, `components/closet/item-detail.tsx:10-16`, `components/closet/closet-grid.tsx:8` `CATEGORIES` / `SEASONS` / `FORMALITY_LABEL` / 14-entry `MATERIALS` are copy-pasted across three files and will drift. **Fix:** derive categories/seasons from `TagSchema` enums (`TagSchema.shape.category.options`) in one shared module, e.g. `lib/closet/vocab.ts`. ### 15. Dead filter logic **Where:** `lib/closet/filter.ts:13` `filterItems` re-checks `archived` client-side though every caller already queries `.eq("archived", false)`, and the `color` filter param has no consumer. **Fix:** reduce it to the category match it actually performs (and its tests along with it). ### 16. Unused motion variants lock in a dead dependency **Where:** `lib/motion.ts:4` `fcRise` / `fcFade` / `fcPop` have zero runtime consumers — only the test imports them, so the suite green-lights an export surface that can silently rot. **Fix:** wire the variants into the shipped screens (capture confirm, closet grid entrances — plan 03 intended this) or drop the module + test until a consumer lands. --- ## Suggested fix order 1. **#1 + #3** (`tag-item.ts` / `tagging-schema.ts`) — one edit session, makes tagging callable 2. **#4** (upload error checks) — 5 lines 3. **#2** (body size limit — quick fix now, client-side upload later) 4. → **e2e-test capture with the API key** (the original next step in STATE.md) 5. **#5, #6, #7** — user-facing polish, each small 6. **#9, #10** — CLAUDE.md compliance (colors editable, tenant tests) 7. **#8, #11–#16** — opportunistic, or fold into plan-06 prep *Not bugs, but open scope from STATE.md: onboarding 5-item capture (plan 04 task 9) not built; `/onboarding` doesn't redirect already-onboarded users away; plan 06 (generator) not started.*

content.text:
Before I write four plans, three things would change what I write. But first, one correction on the materials framing:

**"Ribbed" isn't a material — it's a knit structure.** So the gap isn't a missing enum value, it's a missing *dimension*. What I found:

- `material` in the DB is free text (`items.sql:13`), and the AI can return anything — the prompt suggests "cotton, wool, linen, denim, leather, suede, canvas, knit, metal" and nothing constrains it.
- The 14-entry `MATERIALS` picker is duplicated in `confirm-form.tsx:11` and `item-detail.tsx:13` — two copies that can drift, and neither matches what the tagger emits. That's BUGS.md #14, still open; the `lib/closet/vocab.ts` it proposed was never created.
- There is **no field at all** for texture/knit structure — ribbed, cable, waffle, brushed, fleece-back. Those change how warm and how formal a piece reads, which is exactly the "whole info about clothes" you're missing.

So that plan is really: add a texture dimension, constrain the material vocabulary, unify the pickers, and re-tag existing items (~$0.002 each, so a 100-item closet is 20¢).

On the generator problem — duplicates and skipped items — I'd note that `buildCandidates` picks `outer[0]` and `accessories[0]`, always the *same* first item, and caps combos at 200 in a fixed loop order. That's a plausible mechanism for both symptoms and it's cheap to check now. Happy to leave it until last as you said, just flagging that the cause may already be visible.

content.text:
Three findings, the first of which matters more than the plans themselves.

## `Fitcheck.dc.html` is not a duplicate — it's the whole app design

`docs/STATE.md:82` says `Fitcheck.dc.html` and `generator-mockup-original.html` are "byte-identical duplicates — ignore them." They're not:

```
53c017ba…  Fitcheck.dc.html            116 KB
ebc906d7…  generator-mockup-original   33 KB
8cc5de92…  generator-mockup-v2         33 KB
```

It's 3.5× larger because it's the **complete design, all twelve screens** — and every screen you just asked me to plan is already fully designed in it:

```
ONBOARDING · CLOSET · OUTFIT DETAIL · STYLE DNA · CALENDAR/OOTD
CAPTURE→AI TAG-CONFIRM · ITEM DETAIL · PROFILE HUB · SAVED OUTFITS
WEAR STATS · SETTINGS · BOTTOM TAB BAR
```

We've been building from the generator mockup and a prose summary while the authoritative source sat in the repo marked "ignore". That is very likely the root of "design is mismatching."

## The clothes-data gap is real and specific

`app/closet/[itemId]/actions.ts:9` — `UpdateSchema` accepts `name, brand, category, material, formality, seasons`. Missing:

| Field | State | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `colors` | AI writes it, user can **never** correct it | Wrong colors feed `colorHarmonyScore` directly — a plausible contributor to your "generator picks bad clothes" |
| `pattern` | Same, and the generator never reads it at all | Stripes clash with checks and nothing knows |
| `subcategory` | Same | Item detail can't be corrected |
| `price` | Column exists in `items.sql:16`, **nothing ever writes it** | Cost-per-wear, closet value, and the whole Wear Stats screen are blocked |
| texture | Doesn't exist | Ribbed/cable/waffle has nowhere to live — your original point |

BUGS.md flagged the colors/pattern one on 2026-07-04 as a CLAUDE.md violation ("tags are always user-editable"). It's still open.

The design's item detail also expects `wears`, `lastWorn`, `cost/wear`, a "Goes with" row and a "Style an outfit with this" CTA — none of which exist.

## Proposed slate

| # | Plan | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | seasons-soft-preference | Written, ready |
| 1 | **item data completeness** | colors/pattern/subcategory editable + `texture` field + `price` capture + unified `lib/closet/vocab.ts`. Your materials plan, widened — it's the prerequisite for 2, 3 and 5 |
| 2 | **calendar / OOTD diary** | Needs the wear-log write path; `wear_logs` table already exists |
| 3 | **profile hub** and 4. **settings** | Two plans, as you chose |
| 5 | **generator audit** | Duplicates + skipped items, last before subscription |

Two things I need from you:

1. **Should I pull the remote `Fitcheck.dc.html`?** The project has one at the top level and another inside `design_handoff_stylist_generator/`. Your local copy is from Jul 18 — if you've edited the design since, I'm reading a stale file. Pulling costs a chunk of context, so I'd rather ask than guess.
2. **Which do we brainstorm first?** You picked prototype-review + brainstorm for calendar and profile, so those two want a conversation before I write. Item data completeness I can draft straight away from the design file.

I'd also like to fix that wrong line in `docs/STATE.md` so nobody ignores the design file again — say the word.

| Profile hub | `:659-704` | Stub |
| Settings | `:782-823` | Absent |
| Wear stats | `:737-782` | Absent |
| Saved outfits | `:704-737` | Absent |
| Style DNA | `:367-436` | Absent |
| Outfit detail | `:318-367` | Absent |

---

## 7. Recommended order

1. **Item data completeness** — §4 plus §1.5/1.6 and §2.1/2.2. Unblocks item detail, wear stats and
   the calendar, and plausibly improves generator output by fixing the colour data that feeds ranking.
2. **Item detail rebuild** — §1. Depends on 1 and on wear logs.

4. **Profile hub**, then **Settings**.

Two documents written.

## `docs/design-review-2026-07-24.md`

Design pulled via DesignSync and verified **byte-identical** to your repo copy — so the local file is current and nothing has drifted remotely since Jul 18.

The review covers the five built screens. Headline findings:

- **Item detail is inverted.** The design is a read-first view — Times worn / Cost per wear / Last worn, a "Goes with" row, and a "Style an outfit with this" CTA. Ours is a bare edit form with none of that. It's not a styling gap, it's a different screen.
- **Capture-confirm has no colour field at all**, and never shows the subcategory the AI just read. The design leads with an "AI detected" kicker over the subcategory, with a colour swatch beside material. Also no Retake button — a bad photo can only be escaped by backing out.
- **The tab bar** should be a floating glass pill (22px radius, blur+saturate, drop shadow); ours is a flat full-width bar. Most visible shell deviation.
- **Capture is the least prominent thing on the closet screen** — a small header `+` where the design has a 60px rust FAB.

One divergence I'd keep: our formality control is five 44px buttons vs the design's 8px bars. The design's target is well under the WCAG 2.2 minimum. Noted as justified rather than filed as a defect.

I was explicit about coverage limits: onboarding isn't meaningfully diffable from the static file (its copy is data-bound), and **no screenshots were taken** — every finding is source-to-source, so the purely visual ones should be confirmed in the simulator before acting.

## `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-24-item-data-completeness.md`

Nine TDD tasks. The scoping decision worth flagging: I folded colours/pattern/subcategory/price in with the vocab+texture work because they all touch the same four files — splitting would edit `confirm-form.tsx`, `item-detail.tsx`, vocab and `UpdateSchema` twice. Your option 3 (texture in the generator) is a separate plan, since it can't be tested until texture data exists.

Two things surfaced while writing it:

- **A cycle to avoid.** `vocab.ts` derives `CATEGORIES`/`SEASONS` from `TagSchema`, so `MATERIALS`/`TEXTURES` have to be defined in `tagging-schema.ts` and re-exported — not the other way round.
- **`UpdateSchema` has to move** to `lib/closet/update-schema.ts`. It's currently inside a `"use server"` module, which can only export async functions, so it's untestable where it sits. Same constraint that forces `currentSeason` to move in the seasons plan.

The backfill deliberately does *not* auto-re-tag for texture. That pass costs money per item, and running it accidentally is worse than leaving texture null — which every consumer treats as "no opinion" anyway.

On brainstorming: given the design file specs the calendar (`:436-479`), profile hub (`:659-704`) and settings (`:782-823`) in full detail, I think those need **less** brainstorming than we assumed — the open questions are behavioural (does the calendar auto-log worn looks, or is logging explicit?) rather than "what does this screen look like". Short answer: **no — not from the plan I just wrote.** That plan only fixes the *data*. What you're showing is the item-detail rebuild, which I scoped as the next plan, not this one.

Here's what those two screens need, and where each piece stands:

| Element in the shot | Status |
|---|---|
| `HARTLEY` / **Brushed Oxford** / `Oxford shirt · Cream` | Data comes from plan 1 (subcategory + colour). Rendering is plan 2 |
| **29** TIMES WORN | ❌ `wear_logs` table exists, **nothing ever writes to it** |
| **£3.28** COST / WEAR | ❌ Needs price (plan 1) ÷ wear count (nothing). Also no currency setting anywhere |
| **10 days ago** LAST WORN | ❌ Same wear-log gap |
| FORMALITY bars + "Smart casual" | ✅ Data exists, just needs the read-only display |
| Category / Colour / Material / Seasons rows | ✅ After plan 1 |
| **GOES WITH** carousel | ❌ No complementary-items query exists at all |
| **Style an outfit with this** | ❌ The generator has no "build around this item" input |

One detail in the shot is a good confirmation: the material reads **"Brushed cotton"** — that's exactly the split I put in plan 1. `Brushed` is a texture, `Cotton` is a material, and the display composes them. Without the texture field you'd have to store the literal string "Brushed cotton" as a material, which is what breaks the weather matching. So the design agrees with that call.

**One conflict worth deciding before I write plan 2.** "Style an outfit with this" contradicts Decision 5 — looks are a daily drop, generated once per day; tapping an occasion reads stored rows and never calls the model. But styling around a specific item is inherently an on-demand generation. So: does that button spend an AI call every tap? Does it consume the regenerate quota? Or does it filter the *already-stored* looks down to ones containing this item — and show nothing when none do? That's a genuine fork, and it decides whether the button is cheap or is your biggest per-user cost.

Also note the edit form disappears entirely in this design — everything moves behind the `⋯`. So plan 2 isn't "add stats to the current screen", it's "invert it": read view by default, editing behind the overflow. Worth knowing before I write it, because it changes what plan 1's UI work should target — I'd want plan 1 to put the new controls somewhere that survives the inversion rather than styling a form that plan 2 deletes.

Want me to write plan 2 next, and should I ask you the "Style an outfit with this" question properly before I do?

the source of truth.

what it depends on that does not exist yet.

420px flat-lay hero over a radial gradient · floating glass back button · `OCCASION · WEATHER` kicker ·
serif 34px title · **stylist note** in a rust-bordered card with the rust `f` glyph and the italic serif
quote (the Italic Why Rule) · **"In this look"** piece rows (46px thumb, brand kicker, name, category on
the right) · action bar: bookmark **save** toggle + primary **"Wear this today"** (`detail.wearLabel` is
dynamic, so it toggles to a worn state).

> writes a wear. Times worn, cost/wear, last worn, the calendar grid, streaks, most-worn and
> gathering-dust all read from what this button writes. **It is the correct first build**, not the

number bottom-right; an unlogged day shows just the number; today gets a ring. Italic footnote card
at the bottom.

Depends on: wear logs (§6.1), a streak computation, month navigation (the design shows one month with
no visible control — worth resolving).

### 6.4 Profile hub — `:659-702`

Initials avatar (62px) + name + **handle** · stat trio card · **archetype card** with palette swatches
that taps through to Style DNA · four link rows (icon tile, label, description, chevron) ·
**Fitcheck Pro card**.

### 6.5 Saved outfits — `:704-735`

Back + "Outfits" + a **3-tab segmented control**. Cards are horizontal: a 122px collage panel on the
left, then occasion kicker, serif title, italic note, and a **heart favourite toggle** top-right.
Italic empty state.

Depends on: outfit persistence beyond the daily drop (saved / favourite / worn are three different
states — today `outfits` rows are only the daily drop and are never marked).

# Design vs. Implementation Review — 2026-07-24

**Source of truth:** `design_handoff_stylist_generator/Fitcheck.dc.html` — pulled fresh from the
Claude Design project *Styling* (`82e712a7-45de-4bb2-8414-a6b17e0757f7`) via DesignSync and verified
**byte-identical** to the repo copy (`md5 53c017ba2c75c1c4dc24811bce13151e`). The local file is current;
no design changes have been made remotely since 2026-07-18.

**Excluded by request:** the Stylist / Generate screen. It was built from `generator-mockup-v2.html`
with deliberate, documented divergences and is considered close to right.

---

## 0. The finding that explains the rest

`docs/STATE.md:82` states that `Fitcheck.dc.html` and `generator-mockup-original.html` are
"**byte-identical duplicates** — ignore them."

They are not duplicates, and the instruction to ignore the file is the likely root cause of the
drift being reviewed here:

| File | MD5 | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `Fitcheck.dc.html` | `53c017ba…` | **116 KB** |
| `generator-mockup-original.html` | `ebc906d7…` | 33 KB |
| `generator-mockup-v2.html` | `8cc5de92…` | 33 KB |

`Fitcheck.dc.html` is 3.5× larger because it is the **complete twelve-screen app design**:

```
ONBOARDING · CLOSET · OUTFIT DETAIL · STYLE DNA · CALENDAR/OOTD · CAPTURE→AI TAG-CONFIRM
ITEM DETAIL · PROFILE HUB · SAVED OUTFITS · WEAR STATS · SETTINGS · BOTTOM TAB BAR
```

Every screen still to be built is fully specified in it. **`docs/STATE.md:79-83` must be corrected.**

**Of the twelve designed screens, five are built** (onboarding, closet, capture-confirm, item detail,
tab bar) and can therefore *mismatch*. The other seven are stubs or absent — for those the design is
plan input, not a defect. That is covered in §6.

---

## 1. Item Detail — the largest mismatch

**Design:** `Fitcheck.dc.html:587-657` · **Implementation:** `components/closet/item-detail.tsx`

The information architecture is inverted. The design is a **read-first detail view** that shows what
you own and how you wear it, with editing behind a `⋯` overflow menu. The implementation is a **bare
edit form** with no read view at all — every field is an input, and none of the value the screen
exists to deliver is present.

| # | Design | Implementation | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | Wear-stat trio: **Times worn · Cost/wear · Last worn** (`:604-617`) | Absent | The screen's headline value. Needs `wear_logs` reads + `items.price` |
| 1.2 | **"Goes with"** — horizontal row of 5 complementary pieces (`:641-649`) | Absent | The discovery loop back into the generator |
| 1.3 | Primary CTA **"Style an outfit with this"** (`:654`) | Absent | The only path from an item back to the stylist |
| 1.4 | Tag rows as a read card: Category · Colour · Material · Seasons (`:631-638`) | Six form inputs | — |
| 1.5 | Brand kicker → serif 30px name → `sub · colorName` (`:599-601`) | Two text inputs, **subcategory shown nowhere** | Subcategory is captured then hidden |
| 1.6 | Colour as a named value in the tag rows | `Colours: a · b` muted text (`:173-175`), **not editable** | See §4 |
| 1.7 | Hero: 360px radial-gradient stage (`:595`) | `aspect-[1.3]` flat surface box (`:94`) | Visual |
| 1.8 | Floating glass back `‹` + overflow `⋯` over the hero (`:590-593`) | Inline text `‹`, no overflow menu (`:86-92`) | Visual |
| 1.9 | Sticky bottom bar: `♺` archive icon + primary CTA (`:652-655`) | Text link "Remove from closet" at page end (`:186-192`) | Visual |

**Also, a live data-integrity bug** (`item-detail.tsx:61-63`) — still open from `docs/BUGS.md` #7:

```ts
material: material || "Unknown",
seasons: seasons.length ? seasons : ["Spring"],
```

Clearing the material writes the literal string `"Unknown"`; deselecting every season silently writes
`["Spring"]`. The capture flow guards this same operation differently, so the two screens disagree.

---

## 2. Capture → AI tag-confirm

**Design:** `Fitcheck.dc.html:527-583` · **Implementation:** `components/capture/confirm-form.tsx`

| # | Design | Implementation | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | **Colour** field — hex swatch + colour name, side-by-side with Material (`:548-560`) | **No colour field at all** | AI colour is never reviewed or corrected — and it feeds `colorHarmonyScore` directly |
| 2.2 | "AI detected" gold kicker → serif 26px **subcategory** → `brand · name` (`:537-539`) | Two plain inputs; subcategory never shown | Loses the "the AI read your garment" moment the confirm screen exists for |
| 2.3 | Green **"Background removed"** pill on the cutout (`:532-535`) | Absent | The cutout succeeded and nothing says so |
| 2.4 | Cutout on a 198px radial-gradient stage (`:530`) | Flat `aspect-[1.3]` box (`:35`) | Visual |
| 2.5 | Sticky bar: **Retake** + rust **Add to closet** (`:579-582`) | Single cream button, not sticky, **no Retake** (`:130-136`) | A bad photo can only be fixed by backing out |
| 2.6 | Formality: 5 thin 8px bars (`:568`) | 5 numbered 44px buttons (`:90-105`) | **Justified divergence** — an 8px bar is far below the 24px WCAG 2.2 target minimum. Keep ours; note it |

---

## 3. Closet & shell

**Closet design:** `:157-196` · **Implementation:** `app/closet/page.tsx`, `components/closet/closet-grid.tsx`

Closest of the built screens. The masonry grid (`columns-2`), the brand-kicker-over-name card, and the
`{count} PIECES` / "The Closet" header all match.

| # | Design | Implementation | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3.1 | **Floating rust FAB**, 60px, bottom-right above the tab bar, camera icon (`:192-194`) | Small cream `+` circle in the header (`page.tsx:37-44`) | Capture is the primary action; the design gives it the most prominent element on the screen and ours is the least |
| 3.2 | **Search** button in the header (`:166-168`) | Absent | No way to find a piece in a large closet |
| 3.3 | Card background `linear-gradient(160deg,#1c1b1e,#161517)` (`:181`) | Flat surface | Visual |
| 3.4 | Masonry heights follow image aspect | Cycling array `HEIGHTS = [160,190,…]` (`closet-grid.tsx:10`) | Heights are arbitrary, not content-derived |

**Tab bar design:** `:823-835` · **Implementation:** `components/shell/mobile-nav.tsx`

| # | Design | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| 3.5 | **Floating glass pill** — `border-radius:22px`, `rgba(24,23,26,.82)`, `backdrop-filter:blur(18px) saturate(160%)`, inset hairline + `0 10px 30px` drop shadow, inside a gradient fade, 26px bottom inset (`:825-826`) | Full-width square sticky bar, top border, `bg-canvas/90 backdrop-blur` (`:20`) |

The floating pill is a signature element of the "Midnight Atelier" look and reads as premium; the
current flat bar is the most visible single deviation in the shell.

---

## 4. The clothes-data gap (the "we skipped a lot of info" complaint)

`UpdateSchema` (`app/closet/[itemId]/actions.ts:9-16`) accepts only
`name, brand, category, material, formality, seasons`.

| Field | DB | AI writes | User can edit | Used by generator | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `colors` | ✅ `items.sql:12` | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ `colorHarmonyScore` | **Worst gap** — drives ranking, uncorrectable |
| `pattern` | ✅ `:13` | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ never read | Dead column; design shows it nowhere either |
| `subcategory` | ✅ `:11` | ✅ | ❌ | re-rank text only | Captured, hidden, uneditable |
| `price` | ✅ `:16` ("enables cost-per-wear") | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | **Nothing ever writes it** — blocks §1.1, Wear Stats, closet value |
| texture (ribbed, cable, waffle, brushed) | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | Doesn't exist. A ribbed knit reads warmer and more casual than a flat one |
| `material` | ✅ | ✅ free text | ✅ free text | exact-match in `weatherRules` | Unconstrained both ends; `"merino wool"` ≠ `"wool"` |

`CLAUDE.md` states: *"Tags are always user-editable — treat AI tags as a draft, corrections as free
prompt-tuning signal."* Colours, pattern and subcategory violate this. `docs/BUGS.md` #9 raised it on
2026-07-04; it is still open twenty days later.

**Vocabulary is also triplicated** — `MATERIALS`, `CATEGORIES`, `SEASONS` and `FORMALITY_LABEL` are
copy-pasted in `confirm-form.tsx:8-14` and `item-detail.tsx:10-16`, and neither list matches what the
tagger is told to emit (`lib/ai/tag-item.ts:24-26`). `docs/BUGS.md` #14 proposed `lib/closet/vocab.ts`;
it was never created.

---

## 5. Coverage limits of this review

State plainly what was **not** checked:

- **Onboarding** was not compared in detail. Its copy is data-bound (`{{ }}` props) in the design file,
  so a static diff shows nothing useful — it needs a visual comparison against

- The **Stylist screen was excluded** by request.

---

| Screen | Design | Current |
|---|---|---|
| Calendar / OOTD | `:436-479` | Stub ("Coming soon") |
| Profile hub | `:659-704` | Stub |
| Settings | `:782-823` | Absent |
| Wear stats | `:737-782` | Absent |
| Saved outfits | `:704-737` | Absent |
| Style DNA | `:367-436` | Absent |
| Outfit detail | `:318-367` | Absent |

---

## 7. Recommended order

1. **Item data completeness** — §4 plus §1.5/1.6 and §2.1/2.2. Unblocks item detail, wear stats and

2. **Item detail rebuild** — §1. Depends on 1 and on wear logs.

## 9. The visual system — design values vs. our tokens

Extracted from the inline styles in `Fitcheck.dc.html` (every value is literal in the file) and diffed
against `app/globals.css`. **The token layer is largely faithful** — 15 of the 16 most-used colours map
exactly. The gaps below are systematic, not per-screen, so fixing them improves every surface at once.

### 9.1 Colour — one missing step in the cream ramp

| Design hex | Uses | Our token |
|---|---|---|
| `#ede6d8` | 61 | `--foreground` ✅ |
| `#615c52` | 45 | `--color-muted-dim` ✅ |
| `#928c7f` | 39 | `--muted-foreground` ✅ |
| `#0e0e10` | 28 | `--color-canvas` ✅ |
| `#b86a47` | 27 | `--color-brand` ✅ |
| `#161517` | 27 | `--color-surface-1` ✅ |
| **`#cfc8ba`** | **13** | ❌ **no token** |
| `#19181b` | 12 | `--color-surface-2` ✅ |
| `#52504a` | 8 | `--color-faint` ✅ |
| `#b89a6a` `#6e6f52` `#2c3a4c` | 6 each | `--color-dna-*` ✅ |
| `#201f22` | 5 | `--color-surface-3` ✅ |
| `#d69873` | 5 | `--color-brand-high` ✅ |

**`#cfc8ba` is the design's "value" colour** — the right-hand side of every tag row, item names in
list rows, the material and colour readouts. Our ramp jumps straight from `#ede6d8` (foreground) to
`#928c7f` (muted-foreground), so every value-vs-label pairing is rendered either too bright or too dim.
The design's full cream ramp is eight steps — `#f3eee3 · #ede6d8 · #d9d2c4 · #cfc8ba · #b6ab94 ·
#928c7f · #615c52 · #52504a` — and we have five, missing the middle. **Add `--color-value: #cfc8ba`.**

### 9.2 Surfaces are gradients, not flat fills

The design never fills a card with a flat colour. Ours always does.

| Surface | Design |
|---|---|
| Item / outfit card | `linear-gradient(160deg,#1c1b1e,#161517)` |
| Hero / cutout stage | `radial-gradient(120% 90% at 50% 24%,#201f22,#0e0e10 80%)` |
| Weather strip | `linear-gradient(120deg,#1a191c,#151417)` |
| Rust CTA card | `linear-gradient(120deg,#b86a47,#9a5236)` |
| Archetype card | `radial-gradient(120% 120% at 82% 8%,#241d18,#161517)` |

None of the gradient endpoints (`#1c1b1e`, `#151417`, `#141315`, `#191518`, `#241d18`) are tokenized.
This is the mechanism behind finding 3.3 — it is not "the card colour is slightly off", it is that the
design's depth comes from directional gradients we are not drawing at all.

### 9.3 Hairlines — the design has seven weights, we have two

Every raised surface carries `inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(237,230,216,α)`, with α chosen by elevation:

```
.03 ×1   .05 ×17   .06 ×10   .07 ×5   .08 ×9   .1 ×4   .12 ×4
```

We expose exactly two — `--border` at `.07` and `--input` at `.12`. So a card that should sit at `.05`
renders at `.07`: every panel edge in the app is slightly heavier than designed, and the elevation
hierarchy those seven steps encode is flattened to one. **Expose the ramp as tokens.**

### 9.4 Radii — this one matches

Dominant: `14px` ×19, `13px` ×9, `12px` ×8, `16px` ×7, plus `999px` pills ×24 and `50%` circles ×26.
Our `--radius: 0.875rem` **is** 14px — the design's most-used value. No change needed.

### 9.5 Type — and a tension to resolve

Frequency: `11px` ×26, `10px` ×22, `13px` ×19, `18px` ×14, `14px` ×13, `30px` ×12. Serif display sizes:
`26 · 30 · 34 · 54 · 72`.

**The 10–11px sizes are 48 of the file's font-size declarations** — they are the uppercase,
letterspaced kickers (`letter-spacing:.16em`–`.24em`) that carry the editorial voice. The impeccable
hook currently flags exactly these as "off-ramp font sizes" in `refine-sheet.tsx`, `stylist-view.tsx`
and `item-card.tsx`.

Both positions are defensible and they conflict: uppercase + wide letterspacing is genuinely legible at
10px, and it is the design's signature — but it is also below what our own design-system guide permits,
and small text is an accessibility question we said we'd take seriously (WCAG 2.2 AA is the stated
target in `PRODUCT.md`). **This needs a decision, not a silent default.** Right now we are half-following
each: the design's sizes are in the code, and the linter complains about them on every run.

# Plans

_Reorganised 2026-07-24._ Three folders, one rule: **a plan moves to `done/` only when its work is
merged to `main`** — not when the plan is written, and not when the branch is green.

| Folder | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `todo/` | Written, **not yet implemented**. Execute in the order below. |
| `done/` | Implemented and merged to `main`. Kept for history — the decisions in them are still the record of *why* the code looks the way it does. |
| `scoping/` | Not TDD plans. Research and scoping documents that need a design decision before a plan can be written. |

## Execution order (`todo/`)

The order comes from `docs/design-review-2026-07-24.md` §8. It changed on 2026-07-24 when the full
design review showed that the "Wear this today" button on outfit detail is the only wear-log write path
in the entire product — six other surfaces read what it writes, so it moves near the front.

| # | Plan | Blocks | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `2026-07-24-seasons-soft-preference.md` | — | Independent. A season tag can currently zero every outfit. |
| 2 | `2026-07-24-design-tokens.md` | every screen built after it | Small. Cream ramp, surface gradients, hairline scale. |
| 3 | `2026-07-24-item-data-completeness.md` | 4, 5, 6, 8 | Colours/texture/pattern/price editable; one vocabulary. |
| 4 | `2026-07-24-outfit-detail-wear-logging.md` | 5, 6, 7 | **The unblocker.** Nothing that reads wears can be tested until this exists. |
| 5 | `2026-07-24-item-detail-rebuild.md` | — | Read-first view. Needs 3 + 4. ⚠️ open decision — see below. |
| 6 | `2026-07-24-fit-diary.md` | — | A view over 4. |
| 7 | `2026-07-24-profile-hub.md` → `2026-07-24-settings.md` | — | |
| 8 | `2026-07-24-item-signals-in-generator.md` | — | Texture/pattern in scoring. Needs 3. |
| 9 | `2026-07-22-cutout-backfill.md` | — | One-off script; independent of everything. |
| 10 | `2026-07-22-regenerate-quota.md` | — | ⚠️ Rewrite against the design's actual pricing — `£5/mo`, "unlimited daily looks, packing mode & cost-per-wear analytics" (`Fitcheck.dc.html:697`). "Packing mode" appears in no spec we have. |
| 11 | `2026-07-24-wear-stats.md` | — | ⚠️ Contains two unplanned pieces of scope — see below. |
| 12 | `2026-07-22-route-url-audit.md` | — | **Runs last.** Reworks `/generate`→`/today`, occasion in the URL, `/outfits/[id]`, manifest. Touching routes before the screens exist means doing it twice. |
| 13 | `2026-07-24-generator-audit.md` | — | Duplicates + skipped items. Deliberately last, before subscription work. |

## Open decisions blocking a plan

- **"Style an outfit with this"** (item detail, `Fitcheck.dc.html:654`) conflicts with Decision 5: looks
  are a daily drop, generated once per day, and tapping never calls the model. Styling around a chosen
  item is inherently on-demand. Does it spend an AI call per tap, consume the regenerate quota, or just
  filter the already-stored looks to ones containing that item? This decides whether the button is free
  or is the biggest per-user cost in the product.
- **Wear Stats gap analysis** — *"unlocks 14 new outfits"* is a simulation of what a hypothetical item
  would enable, not a query. Needs designing.
- **"See curated picks"** (`:767`) — a commerce/affiliate surface with no product decision behind it.
- **Small type** — the design uses 10–11px for its uppercase kickers, which our design-system guide
  flags. **Deferred to the end of the project** by decision on 2026-07-24; do not spend time on it.

## Not in the queue

- `scoping/2026-07-24-womens-wardrobe-scoping.md` — the one-piece-garment (dress/jumpsuit) fork.
  Deliberately deferred: "womens a lot later".
- The occasion learner — waiting on real `occasion_overrides` data.

## Source of truth for anything visual

`design_handoff_stylist_generator/Fitcheck.dc.html` — the complete twelve-screen design, verified
against the Claude Design project *Styling* on 2026-07-24. Two identical copies also exist at
`styling/project/Fitcheck.dc.html` and inside the design-handoff folder. `docs/STATE.md` previously
described this file as a duplicate to ignore; that was wrong and is the root cause of the drift
catalogued in `docs/design-review-2026-07-24.md`.

**Read `docs/superpowers/plans/README.md` first** — it is the execution index and it explains the
folder structure. Then `docs/design-review-2026-07-24.md`. Current as of 2026-07-24.

## The big correction of 2026-07-24

`design_handoff_stylist_generator/Fitcheck.dc.html` is **not** a duplicate of the generator mockup.
It is the **complete twelve-screen app design** (116 KB vs 33 KB, different MD5), verified byte-identical
to the Claude Design project *Styling* (`82e712a7-45de-4bb2-8414-a6b17e0757f7`) via the DesignSync tool.
`docs/STATE.md:79-83` calls it a "byte-identical duplicate — ignore them", which is wrong and is the
root cause of the UI drift. Onboarding — the one screen built *from* this file — is also the one screen
that matches. Two more identical copies exist: `styling/project/Fitcheck.dc.html` and the one inside the
handoff folder. **Fixing that STATE.md paragraph is a step inside the item-data-completeness plan.**

## Plans are now organised, not a flat pile

`docs/superpowers/plans/{todo,done,scoping}/` + `README.md` as the index. A plan moves to `done/` only
when its work is **merged to main**. 14 in `todo/`, 7 in `done/`, 1 scoping doc.

Ten plans were written on 2026-07-24 — all of `todo/2026-07-24-*`. Execution order lives in the README;
the short version: seasons → design-tokens → item-data → **outfit-detail+wear-logging (the unblocker)**
→ item-detail-rebuild → fit-diary → profile-hub → settings → item-signals → wear-stats →
route-url-audit (last) → generator-audit.

## Why outfit-detail moved to the front

The "Wear this today" button (`Fitcheck.dc.html:362`) is the **only wear-log write path in the entire
design**. Times worn, cost-per-wear, last worn, the Fit Diary grid, streaks, most-worn and
gathering-dust are all views over it, and nothing writes `wear_logs` today. The calendar cannot be built
first — it would be an empty grid.

## Two latent bugs found by reading, not yet fixed

1. **Wear + regenerate = foreign-key violation.** `wear_logs.outfit_id` has no `ON DELETE` action and
   `saveDailyLooks` is delete-then-insert. Unreachable only because nothing writes wear logs yet. Fixed
   by the outfit-detail plan (nulls `generated_on` to graduate a worn look out of the daily drop).
2. **The generator can only reach one top.** `buildCandidates` builds a top-major nested product then
   slices to `CAP = 200`; with 20/20/20 the first top alone makes 800 combos. Explains both of the
   user's reported symptoms (duplicates + skipped clothes) with one line. `outer[0]`/`accessories[0]`
   are pinned too. The generator-audit plan measures before fixing — **do not skip its Task 1.**

## Decisions made 2026-07-24

- **WCAG / small-type question is DEFERRED to the end of the project.** The design uses 10–11px for its
  uppercase kickers and the impeccable hook flags them. Do not spend time on it.
- **Women's wardrobe is deferred** ("a lot later"). Scoping doc only.
- **Pro is £5/mo** — from the design itself (`:698`, `:797`): *"Unlimited daily looks, packing mode &
  cost-per-wear analytics."* **"Packing mode" appears in no spec we have.** The queued regenerate-quota
  plan should be rewritten against this.
- Prices are GBP for now; a currency setting belongs to Settings.

## Open decision blocking one plan

**"Style an outfit with this"** (item detail) contradicts the daily-drop model. The item-detail-rebuild
plan assumes the cheap reading — filter today's stored looks, and only spend a quota-consuming
generation if none contain the item — and says so at the top. Confirm or overturn before implementing.

## Merged to `main`

daily-drop (#9) · WebP cutouts (#10) · CI (#11) · signed-URL cache (#12) · smart-default-occasion (#13,
merged 2026-07-24 08:18). Local `main` may be a commit behind; `feat/smart-default-occasion` still
exists locally and remotely and can be deleted.

## How to work here

Branch → PR → CI `verify` green → merge; `main` is protected. TDD every change. Verify UI in the
**iOS Simulator** (iPhone 17), never a resized browser — [[mobile-first-evaluate-at-phone-width]],
[[live-verify-ui-work]]. `xcrun simctl` is broken; use
`/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr/bin/simctl`. No AI attribution anywhere
([[no-ai-attribution]]). Small scoped plans ([[prefer-multiple-scoped-plans]]), future-proof at forks
([[prefer-future-proof-architecture]]).

See [[fitcheck-project]], [[daily-drop-model]], [[womens-wardrobe-gap]], [[future-occasion-learner]].
